answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making each identity earn trust through costly, verifiable work: a new agent starts as a cold ember with no reputation and must complete attested tasks before it can transact. A public beacon service publishes signed proofs of that work, so peers check the beacon record instead of trusting self-claims. Forging thousands of fake identities then costs real compute and time, leaving the attacker stranded on a tundra of empty, unproven accounts, while honest agents accumulate durable credit that cannot be copied.
